parameters.atmosphere: Ti-gettered argon; remelted at least five times
parameters.cooling_method: rapidly dropped into a water-cooled copper mold

evidence.quote: The samples were prepared by vacuum arc melting in a Ti-gettered argon atmosphere. The ingots were flipped over and remelted at least five times for chemical homogeneity and then rapidly dropped into a water-cooled copper mold with dimension of 100 × 12 × 5 mm3.
The as-cast ingots were first homogenized at 1200 ◦C for 2 h to reduce solute segregation.

parameters.deformation: 30% total thickness reduction along the longitudinal direction

evidence.quote: Then the sample was subjected to cold rolling along the longitudinal direction with a total thickness reduction of 30%
followed by recrystallization at 1200 ◦C for 20 min.
Subsequently, aging treatment was applied in the 10% predeformed (to accelerate the precipitate kinetics) sample at 700 ◦C for 1 hour.

Subsequently, aging treatment was applied in the 10% predeformed (to accelerate the precipitate kinetics) sample at 700 ◦C for 1 hour. Air cooling were adopted in all the heat treatment procedures to avoid cracks.

the existence of a dense L12 phase benefits anomalous hardening and high strength by hindering the motion of dislocations [37], which ensures the high strength of the FCC matrix in the HESA at elevated temperatures

Owing to the different crystalline structures, there is strong strain partitioning between the FCC and B2 matrix. To accommodate the strain gradients, geometrically necessary dislocations will block and pile up at the phase boundary [45], generating long-range back stress and making dislocations hard to move in the FCC matrix.

mechanisms.name: crack nucleation suppression at serrated phase boundary

evidence.quote: The existence of the B2 phase with a serrated phase boundary suppresses the nucleation and propagation of cracks, leading to high ductility at elevated temperatures.

mechanisms.name: crack propagation blocking at serrated phase boundary

evidence.quote: their bridging and propagation were blocked (Fig. 4 (d)) because the zigzag array of the cavity formed at the SPB makes it more difficult to interlink and compose an intergranular path for crack propagation

mechanisms.name: dislocation pile-up strengthening at phase boundary

evidence.quote: high-density dislocations piled up at both sides of the phase boundary, indicating its strengthening effect
